title: Pricing Bulletin: Multi-System Discount on Replacement System Installations Signed the Same Day
content:
# Multi-system discount — Replacement System Installations

## Rule

When a homeowner signs two or more Replacement System Installations contracts for the same service address on the same signing date, the contract with the highest contract price is the first system, and every other contract signed that day receives a multi-system discount equal to its own package's multi-system discount percentage of its own contract price, rounded to the cent half up and naming that contract's contract-price charge. The discount is posted once per qualifying contract.

Contracts signed on different days never qualify, even when they are installed together. A qualifying contract that is later cancelled keeps no discount, because its charges are credited in full under the cancellation rules.

## Basis of judgement

The qualification is read from the system records of the projects: the homeowner on each contract, each contract's signing date and each contract's contract price. The discount is tied to the project that receives it, and the project's ledger shows whether a multi-system discount has already been posted on it.

## Condition table

| Same homeowner, same service address | Same signing date | Contract | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | Highest contract price of that day | First system — no multi-system discount |
| Yes | Yes | Any other contract of that day | Multi-system discount on its own contract price |
| Yes | No (different days) | Any | Does not qualify |

## Worked example (hypothetical contracts)

A homeowner signs two contracts for one address on the same day: a hypothetical contract at $14695.00 and another at $10695.00, both on packages whose multi-system discount percentage is 5 percent.

1. The $14695.00 contract has the highest contract price, so it is the first system and receives no multi-system discount.
2. The $10695.00 contract receives 5 percent of $10695.00, which is $534.75, naming its own contract-price charge.

Had the second contract been signed the following day, neither contract would qualify, whatever their installation dates.
